title: Transaction approval, rejection and completion
prerequisites: These bindings target classic MCSDK with KSSIDP; standalone IDPSDK needs its own adapter and is not interchangeable.
User/device activated and authenticated as required by deployment.
Backend TMS initiation targets that device/user; app event listener active.

Mandatory agent gate: before activation call sdk_deployment_preflight(mc_config_path, expected_mtls) using actual configuration and explicit customer deployment choice, never a sample default. Explicit-auth TMS always requires require_explicit_authentication=true and expected_token_client from observed token ownership. Set granted_scope_stage=current (default) for the existing token: missing tms warns/pends verification, NOT blocks, because SDK StartTransaction may acquire it through exchange/step-up. Set granted_scope_stage=explicit_auth for the actual resulting token: granted_scopes must contain tms, otherwise missing scope/evidence blocks. Requested/assigned scopes are not actual granted-token evidence. The tool verifies supplied metadata only (configuration_checked, runtime acceptance false), not issuer capability, live token validity or backend acceptance; no policy enforcement on independent raw service API calls.

Explicit-authentication scope tms is necessary for the observed AST check, not sufficient proof of fresh user/device authentication. Preserve require_explicit_authentication=true. Never turn it off or blindly create/grant a realm scope to pass; establish the documented step-up/mapper/token-issuance contract first. Keep the selected themed WebView clients; reconcile app-local IAM exchange identity with the actual token holder rather than guessing from login-client naming. A token endpoint HTTP200 or SDK OfflineLogin success does not by itself prove the SignedJWT grant or TMS authorization.
sequence: Handle transaction availability/banner and start retrieval with the SDK transaction-start event.
Display the confirmation request transaction information and remaining time.
Submit the actual user decision through DisplayConfirmation; bind it to the displayed transaction information.
Handle any required authorization-code step for the selected SDK flow.
Wait for the terminal transaction event and inspect status; compare with backend result when testing end-to-end.
expected_result: The displayed transaction reaches a terminal SDK result matching the actual user decision and backend outcome.
checklist: Approve and reject paths both tested.
Expired/cancelled transaction cannot be reported as approved.
Confirmation acknowledgement is not treated as terminal completion.
Displayed information matches the transaction being confirmed.
failure_handling: Do not automate approval of an arbitrary real transaction. Use explicit test transactions.
UI timeout and backend completion may race; inspect final result rather than submitting twice.

errorCode 516004035 presented as generic "A network error occurred" during confirmation can actually be an authentication-FRESHNESS rejection: the backend answered HTTP 403 "The access token is 85 seconds older than required" and the SDK wraps it; the real cause is visible only in the embedded HTTP body of the error (observed 2026-09-29, iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231). Inspect the embedded HTTP body before diagnosing a network problem, and check the trigger's requireFreshnessOfAuthentication value.

requireFreshnessOfAuthentication is evaluated at CONFIRMATION time, not at trigger time: 0 (or values below the confirmation latency) makes every confirmation fail with the 403/516004035 pattern above. Use the sdk_tms_trigger default 3600, a deliberate larger value, or -1 to disable; two device attempts were wasted on this trap before diagnosis (VAL-28 evidence, 2026-09-29).

A not-yet-terminal transaction answers HTTP 412 on the backend result endpoint; sdk_tms_result maps it to an explicit lowercase status "pending" (observed 2026-09-29 during bounded-wait polling). Pending is not a backend error: keep bounded polling and never re-trigger a transaction because its result is still pending.

When SDK reports FAILED/errorCode=0 and no Warning/RuntimeError/FatalError, inspect sanitized native SDK and HTTP diagnostics; listener silence is not absence of an error. Distinguish issuer TLS_CLIENT_WITH_KEY rejection 510000015 (mTLS deployment mismatch), HTTP403 Client is not the holder of the token wrapped as 700000022 (token holder versus IAM exchange client), missing explicit tms scope 516004034, and freshness failure 516004035. Numeric wrappers alone do not establish the cause; retain operation/status/explanation without tokens.

Use sdk_tms_auth_diagnose to distinguish ordinary scope, required transaction scope, requested exchange scope, HTTP result, issued scopes and AST decision. Maverick performs the inspected exchange internally before confirmation; do not invent an extra application WebView step. HTTP200 does not prove tms was issued. Verify the supplied SDK version.

Capture inherited error fields on confirmation and terminal results, including hasErrorOccurred, errorCode, errorDescription and reportId where exposed. Swift status39 can carry detailed server516004034 even when Warning/Runtime/Fatal events are silent.

Compare users under the same exchange client and explicit-authentication policy. No missing ordinary scope alone proves a user-creation defect. Claims lookup may update session lastAccess; this is not transaction-exchange evidence. Do not recreate users or grant default tms scope blindly.

Test timeout and server cancellation independently from accept/reject. Local timeout may complete without a decision PATCH. Older non-explicit passes and disabled legacy SDK tests do not prove current explicit-auth support.

platform_notes.android: StartTransactionEvent → DisplayConfirmationRequestEvent → DisplayConfirmationEvent → DisplayConfirmationResultEvent → TransactionEndEvent in the inspected Shift model.
platform_notes.ios: KSMStartTransactionEvent → KSMDisplayConfirmationRequestEvent → KSMDisplayConfirmationEvent → KSMDisplayConfirmationResultEvent → KSMTransactionFinishedEvent in the inspected model.

qualification.note: Examples compile against the exact classic MCSDK/KSSIDP artifact in each example validation record. Compilation and synthetic diagnostics do not qualify a complete live app flow.
